findings.title: RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK now counts "a working agreement no artefact records" as a check, in the same paragraph that still says remembering a rule is not enforcement
locations: policy/RULES.toml:1-8 (the header defining the check classes) and the 25 rows carrying check = ["panel"] or check = ["session"]
test/schemas.jl:5415-5439 of the diff (the new "every rule declares what catches its next violation" testset)
findings.before: "When a rule is written down, name what would catch its next violation, and if the answer is \"someone remembering this rule\", it is not enforced." (base policy/testing-protocol.md)
findings.after: "name what would catch its next violation in its `RULES.toml` `check` field: a `scan:`, `doctor:` or `test:` id, a `harness:` binding the tool enforces it by, `panel` for a rule only a reading panel can decide, `session` for a working agreement no artefact records, or `weakness` … `panel` and `session` are answers; `weakness` is a debt."
findings.why_it_matters: The rule's whole force was that an unenforced rule must be recorded as a weakness. The edit invents two classes that satisfy the rule without any check existing, and `session` is defined as "a working agreement no artefact records" — exactly "someone remembering this rule", which the very next sentence of the same paragraph still says "is not enforcement". Six rules (RULE.INST.CONSENT, RULE.INST.FIX_FROM_LANES, RULE.GIT.PUSH, RULE.GIT.CI_MANUAL, RULE.GIT.NO_SHIMS, RULE.GIT.REQUESTS) and nineteen more on `panel` are now recorded fleet-wide as having an answer where at base they were, by the rule's own terms, known weaknesses. The RULES.toml statement and sentinel are unchanged ("a stated rule without a check is a known weakness"), so the register still advertises the strong reading. The only new enforcement asserts `!isempty(cs)` and then `c in ("panel", "session", "weakness")` — it verifies that a string is present, never that a check exists.
findings.description: The taxonomy is a reasonable bookkeeping addition, but it was written so that the two new classes are declared "answers". A defensible version records `panel` and `session` as sub-kinds of the debt rather than as satisfaction of it; that would have kept the sentence about remembering intact and left the 25 rows visible as weaknesses. As edited, the rulebook's one self-policing rule can no longer be violated: every rule now declares something, and three of the six declarable values require nothing to be built.
findings.evidence: base: "if the answer is \"someone remembering this rule\", it is not enforced" — head, same paragraph: "`session` for a working agreement no artefact records … `panel` and `session` are answers; `weakness` is a debt." followed two lines later by the surviving "\"Someone remembering this rule\" is not enforcement." RULES.toml:518 statement unchanged: "A rule and its check land in the same commit; a stated rule without a check is a known weakness."

findings.title: RULE.DOC.HOME_ORDER's docstring order reversed fleet-wide, and the new order contradicts RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE's "# References at its end"
findings.before: "A function docstring is ordered: identity, when-to-use, arguments, caveats, one formula, citation, links." … "(4) the caveats a user needs, as an admonition where load-bearing; (5) one formula …; (6) an inline citation …; (7) cross-links."
findings.after: "A function docstring is ordered: identity, when-to-use, arguments, one formula, citation, links, caveats." … "(7) the caveats a user needs, as an admonition where load-bearing — the last substantive block, before the fields list."
findings.why_it_matters: This is a rendered policy file: every consumer pins it and every docstring in the four science packages was written to the base order. The rule's check is recorded as `weakness` — nothing catches a violation — so the divergence surfaces only as panel findings at each consumer's next round. Worse, the new order names only the fields list as coming after the caveats, while RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE (unchanged) requires the full reference "in a `# References` section at its end". A docstring with both a citation and a load-bearing caveat now has two rules each claiming the last block; at base there was no collision, the caveats sitting at (4). The fixture already carries a `# References` docstring section (fixture/GBG Fixture/src/FixtureC.jl:35), so the collision is reachable in the tool's own corpus.
findings.description: The reordering may be defensible, but the change set does not carry the evidence for it and does not carry the consequence. Nothing in this package forced it: the re-baselined docs/prose_shape.csv shows admonitions = 0 on every docstring unit of src/, so the tool's own corpus has no docstring caveat to place. The two personas that would report the divergence — doc-policy and structure-consistency — were rewritten to the new order in the same commit, so the instrument that judges the order and the order it judges moved together. Neither the rule paragraph nor RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE was amended to say which of the two owns the end of a docstring.
findings.evidence: docs-rubric.md head: "(7) the caveats a user needs, as an admonition where load-bearing — the last substantive block, before the fields list." citations.md head (unchanged clause): "A docstring cites author–year in its prose and carries the full reference in a `# References` section at its end". RULES.toml:23: check = ["weakness"].

findings.title: A new binding fleet rule was appended inside RULE.INST.AUDIT_AFTER_CODE's paragraph, with no id, no register statement and a check that tests something else
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl bank(): the new instrument-specific NEXT line
findings.before: "A prose-only pass is not gated: run the audit's prose lenses on judgment when the pass rewrote docstrings that state a contract." — the paragraph ended there.
findings.after: "… that state a contract. An audit round is closed by disposing its concerns, never by correcting them inside it: a correction moves the tree, the staleness check then refuses the close, and there is no re-bank. A correction rides the next change set, which the next audit covers."
findings.why_it_matters: This is a second, independent rule — a prohibition on editing the tree during an audit round — placed inside the paragraph of an unrelated rule about when an audit is required. Its host's RULES.toml statement still reads only "A fix pass that changed code is audited before its round closes: always for a hunt, and for a check-docs round whose pass touched src or ext", so the register the instruments cite does not carry the new prohibition. LEG.SENTINELS matches the paragraph's FIRST sentence and the parity test matches heading against row, so both keep passing and neither notices. The host's check is test:test/rounds.jl, and nothing in that file — including the two testsets this change set adds — exercises the no-correction rule; the new class-declaration test would nonetheless report the rule as checked.
findings.description: The substance may well be right (the staleness check does make a corrected audit round unclosable). The defect is the delivery: a rule that changes how every consumer runs /audit-changes was given no id of its own, no one-line statement, no sentinel and therefore no way for the ledger, the doctor or a scan to reach it, while inheriting a check earned by a different requirement. Compare RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM in this same change set, which was given its own id, statement, sentinel and scan:SCAN.ARGS_FORM.
findings.evidence: policy/instruments.md:41-43 (the appended sentences) against policy/RULES.toml:574 statement = "A fix pass that changed code is audited before its round closes: always for a hunt, and for a check-docs round whose pass touched src or ext." and :576 check = ["test:test/rounds.jl"].

findings.title: SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE's "Caps bind ALWAYS" and the caveat naming re-baselining as the escape were rewritten away — with the scan's code byte-identical, in the change set that re-baselines the CSV wholesale
locations: src/Scans/prose_shape.jl:96-115 (the register body — unchanged at base and head)
findings.before: "Caps bind ALWAYS (longest paragraph ≤ 120 words, ≤ 3 admonitions; IT's lesson: a cap that applies only to new units is escaped by re-baselining or renaming)." / RULES.toml: "… at most 3 admonitions, always; no unit grows past its baseline …" / ARCHITECTURE: "caps 120 words / 3 admonitions always"
findings.after: "Caps (longest paragraph ≤ 120 words, ≤ 3 admonitions) bind on every docstring and every NEW page unit; a page unit already in the baseline is held by the ratchet alone, the one place IT's lesson … is traded for an append-only log." / RULES.toml: "… no unit grows past its baseline, and a page unit already baselined is held by that ratchet alone …" / ARCHITECTURE: "caps … on every docstring and every NEW page unit, a baselined page unit held by the ratchet alone"
findings.why_it_matters: `git show <base>:src/Scans/prose_shape.jl` and the file at head are identical from register_scan! to end: the guard reads `if occursin(" :: ", k) || b === nothing` at both commits. No behaviour was fixed — the promise was moved to fit the code, in three places at once (the scan header, the rule register the consumers pin, and the design's scan table). The quantifier "always" and the recorded lesson that named re-baselining as the escape are the two things a future reader would use to challenge exactly this shape, and the same change set exercises that escape: docs/prose_shape.csv is regenerated wholesale, with the ARCHITECTURE §12.B unit's longest paragraph raised 1208 → 1287 words and §7.3's 1651 → 1672, both far past the cap that no longer binds them.
findings.description: The honest correction is defensible in the scan header, where a comment contradicted the function two lines below it. It is not defensible in policy/RULES.toml, which is rendered into four consumers as the statement of RULE.DOC.SHAPE: there "always" was a promise about the fleet's prose, and dropping it lowers the standard for every consumer's pages without any consumer asking. If the caps genuinely cannot bind a baselined page unit, the entry owed is a ledger deviation or a `weakness`, not a quieter rule. Nothing in the diff records the lesson's loss as a debt.
findings.evidence: Both commits: `if occursin(" :: ", k) || b === nothing` … `u.longest > PROSE_PARAGRAPH_CAP && push!(hits, …)`. Base header: "Caps bind ALWAYS … IT's lesson: a cap that applies only to new units is escaped by re-baselining or renaming". Head CSV row: "ARCHITECTURE.md § §12.B Scan catalogue (`catalog/scans.toml`)",1462,1287,0 where base held 1383,1208,0.

findings.title: SCAN.MATHBF now admits \mathbf{1} whatever the config says, while RULE.TEX.MATHBF's register statement still reads "admitted only for the strings in notation.mathbf_allowed"
findings.before: allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"])) — and the rule: "Never the other, and never an upright `\mathbf` outside the admitted list."
findings.after: allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"])); push!(allowed, "\\mathbf{1}") — and the rule gains: "`\mathbf{1}` … is admitted in every package whatever that list holds; it is not a package's to withhold."
findings.why_it_matters: notation.mathbf_allowed is one of the four values the design says vary by package (docs/src/guide/config.md; ARCHITECTURE §5). A consumer that emptied the list to ban every upright \mathbf got hits on \mathbf{1} at base and gets silence at head — a config value that used to decide now cannot. The register was not moved with it: RULES.toml:357 still states "\\mathbf is admitted only for the strings in notation.mathbf_allowed", and the sentinel LEG.SENTINELS matches is still "`\mathbf` is admitted only for an agreed list of strings". Anything that cites the rule id — a ledger scope = "policy" entry, an instrument's brief, a consumer reading the register — is told the list is the whole answer.
findings.description: The exception is coherent with RULE.TEX.MATHBB, which does name \mathbf{1} as the indicator and identity, and the schema description and the guide page were both updated. What was not done is the register row, which the design (§12.A) makes the one-line authority. Two of the three places that state the rule now say opposite things about whether the config can withhold \mathbf{1}.

findings.title: The tally artefact's `state` vocabulary was widened by four values without §6.3, the design's closed-vocabulary table, being touched
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:398 (entry["state"] = … uppercase(String(r.status)), unchanged in the window)
findings.after: "enum": ["PRESENT", "PARTIAL", "REGRESSED", "ABSENT", "NOT-A-DEFECT", "UNCLEAR", "PASS", "FAIL", "BROKEN", "BLOCKED"] with "description": "a state verifier's verdict, or — on a bug-hunt finding whose witness was re-run — that witness's status"
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md's core invariants and ARCHITECTURE §6.3 make the vocabularies constants: "Changing any vocabulary is MAJOR." §6.3 line 1530 still publishes the state-verdict vocabulary as the six values, and §6.3 closes with "Precondition for every consumer's adoption: before it adopts, audit its tally and adjudication code for closed switches over the old enums — a switch written for the old set silently misreads the new one." A reader following that instruction audits against a list that no longer matches the schema its tallies are validated by. The widening itself looks correct — Passes.jl:398 already wrote witness statuses into `state` at base, so the base schema would have thrown on any real hunt tally — but the design record was not brought along, and neither §6.3 nor the CHANGELOG entry names the enum.
findings.description: A schema widened to admit values the code already produced is the right repair. The drift is that the authoritative vocabulary table is the design document, not the schema file, and only the schema moved. Either §6.3 gains the four values with the note that they arrive from the witness re-run, or the grade path stops overloading `state` with a witness status — but the two cannot say different things while §6.3 is cited as the constant.
findings.evidence: schema/tally.schema.json:177-181 adds "PASS", "FAIL", "BROKEN", "BLOCKED"; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1530 unchanged: "| state verdict | `PRESENT \| PARTIAL(surviving_class) \| REGRESSED \| ABSENT \| NOT-A-DEFECT \| UNCLEAR` |"; the ARCHITECTURE hunks in this diff are at 380, 592, 622, 951, 989, 1113, 1450, 1464, 1628, 1711, 1735, 2175 and 2295 — §6.3 at 1526-1545 is untouched.

findings.title: CFG.SURFACES no longer requires docs_build to name docs/make.jl; the fleet constant was dropped and replaced by a regex over the command string
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1123 (the config example's comment) and :1759 (the CFG.SURFACES row)
test/config.jl:5238-5245 of the diff (the new assertions)
findings.before: isfile(joinpath(root, "docs", "make.jl")) || push!(errs, "package.docs_build: docs/make.jl does not exist"); ARCHITECTURE: "`docs_build` names `docs/make.jl` and that file exists" and "# CFG.SURFACES requires it to name docs/make.jl"
findings.after: scripts = [String(m.match) for m in eachmatch(r"[^\s\"']+\.jl", cfg["package"]["docs_build"])] … isfile(joinpath(root, s)) || push!(errs, …); ARCHITECTURE: "every `.jl` script the `docs_build` command names exists" and "# CFG.SURFACES requires the .jl it names to exist"
findings.why_it_matters: Two contract changes in one edit, and only the second is the stated motive. The motive — check the file the command actually runs — is right. The unstated half is that the requirement that a consumer's docs build BE docs/make.jl is gone fleet-wide; gbg init still seeds docs/make.jl from a template, WIRE.MAKEDOCS still expects the wrapper there, and D9 still names the docs build the per-push enforcement point, so the tool now has one fewer guarantee about where that enforcement lives. In the other direction the check is stricter than base: a consumer with docs/make.jl present but docs_build naming a different script passed CFG.SURFACES at base and fails at head — the new test/config.jl case asserts exactly that refusal.
findings.description: The doc was updated in both places, so this is disclosed rather than silent, which is why it is minor. What is missing is any replacement for the dropped constant: nothing in the change set says whether a consumer may now point docs_build anywhere, or whether docs/make.jl remains required by some other check. The regex is also looser than the prose: [^\s"']+\.jl picks a .jl token out of any part of the command line, including one inside a -e script body, and each such token is then required to exist as a file.
findings.evidence: base src/CLI/Config.jl: isfile(joinpath(root, "docs", "make.jl")) || push!(errs, "package.docs_build: docs/make.jl does not exist"); base ARCHITECTURE:1123 "# CFG.SURFACES requires it to name docs/make.jl"; head test/config.jl asserts any(e -> occursin("build_the_site.jl", e) && occursin("docs_build", e), bad).

findings.title: The comment recording why the fixture must be a test dependency was deleted, and nothing replaced it
locations: src/CLI/Audit.jl:16-18 (where the parallel note for the tool's own path source was added)
findings.before: "# the toy consumer the reflection scans load: without it `load_package` fails and the four reflection scans skip themselves silently, which is how they had never run under `Pkg.test()`" immediately above [sources]
findings.after: the comment is gone; [sources] now reads GBGCodingTools = {path = ".."} then GBGFixture = {path = "../fixture/GBG Fixture"}
findings.why_it_matters: That sentence is the only record in the tree of a failure mode that had already happened once — the four reflection scans skipping themselves silently and reporting clean. With it gone, GBGFixture reads as an ordinary test dependency, and the next person tidying test/Project.toml has nothing telling them that removing it turns four hard scans into silent no-ops rather than into failures. The same change set shows the author knows such a note is worth keeping: the new GBGCodingTools = {path = ".."} entry got its rationale written into src/CLI/Audit.jl's docstring ("without that every claim fails to load it and the audit's account of what runs is built on nothing") — the older entry lost its.
findings.description: Nothing in the edit required removing the comment: the change to this file is the addition of a dep and a source. The deletion is collateral, and it removes a warning rather than a stale claim — the claim is still true at head.
findings.evidence: diff test/Project.toml: "-# the toy consumer the reflection scans load: without it `load_package` fails and the four" / "-# reflection scans skip themselves silently, which is how they had never run under `Pkg.test()`" with no + line carrying it elsewhere in the change set.
